title: Time Jump — 11:00 AM PDT, 46 Minutes After the Earthquake

fields.narration: It is now 11:00 Pacific Daylight Time, 46 minutes after the earthquake. The National Tsunami Warning Center's Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast is still in effect. The Port Alder primary 911 center is under water. Telecommunicators are now on the backup positions here at the Kellerton EOC, and more than 60 calls are waiting. Power is out across the county and the EOC is running on its generator. Cell service comes and goes. The Port Alder tide gauge has sent no data since 10:41. Engine 32 reports that the hospital's non-ambulatory patients are on the Kellerton Fire Station 3 apron. Spruce Hill is crowded with evacuees standing in the rain, and the State Parks ranger is holding about 180 campers on the high bluff. Nobody has seen the harbor since 10:45. Three sirens, at Front Street, the harbor and the campground, are still silent. Since the first wave, news crews and the public have kept calling to ask about the magnitude and how high the water is. The clock is running. Continue.
worldState: Time is 11:00 AM PDT. The earthquake struck at 10:14 AM PDT.
The NTWC Tsunami Warning for the coastal areas of Oregon and Washington remains in effect. The EOC has received no cancellation.
The only observed wave is the one recorded by the Port Alder tide gauge: +2.4 m above predicted tide at 10:38. The gauge has sent no data since 10:41 and no newer water-level readings are available.
Nobody has seen the harbor, the Port Alder waterfront or the Alder River flats since 10:45. Damage there is unknown.
Port Alder primary 911 center: flooded and abandoned. 911 is answering from the backup positions at the Kellerton EOC with more than 60 calls in the queue.

Commercial power is out countywide. The EOC is on its backup generator, which holds 5 days of fuel. Cell service is intermittent. The satellite phone, amateur radio station and two Starlink terminals work.
The Front Street, harbor and campground sirens are still silent. The other sirens sounded.
Marlow Coast Community Hospital: non-ambulatory patients are on the Kellerton Fire Station 3 apron, waiting to move to the EOC medical branch.
Spruce Hill assembly area is crowded and exposed to rain. The State Parks ranger is holding about 180 campers on the high bluff.
The Cedar Court assisted living residents and the boats and workers at the harbor have not reported their status to the EOC.
Media and public calls keep coming in about which magnitude is correct and how high the water got.
The WebEOC Tsunami Status board still reads "Awaiting first arrival" until someone updates it.
fields.facilitatorNote: Expected actions: every position updates its WebEOC board (Tsunami Status should now show the observed 10:38 arrival). Command confirms the XL/XXL evacuation order stays in force, sets the next briefing time and asks each position for a status report based on observations. Probe for: anyone suggesting a return or 'all clear' (the NTWC has not cancelled and the gauge is down, so the conditions for a return order cannot be met); the PIO publishing a wave height or a magnitude other than the latest official figure; and whether Command starts tracking the local emergency declaration, which is due within four hours. If players ask about aftershocks, the USGS has not issued an aftershock forecast yet.

instructorNote: This card opens Phase 2. It is meant to stop the room from relaxing after the first wave. Command should keep the XL/XXL order in force, set the next briefing time and get status reports based on observations from each position. Watch for any talk of returning people while the Warning is still active and the gauge is down.
